hafm-01-c2.text: Cesar A. Fortes-Lima, Concetta Burgarella, Rickard Hammarén, et al (2024). The genetic legacy of the expansion of Bantu-speaking peoples in Africa. Nature 625(7995): 540-547 (epub Nov 2023).
hafm-01-c2.quote: this expansion that started 6,000-4,000 years ago in western Africa.
hafm-01-c2.claim: A 2024 study in Nature led by Cesar Fortes-Lima, which sampled more than 1,500 Bantu speakers, dates the start of the expansion to roughly 6,000 to 4,000 years ago in western Africa.

hafm-04-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Timbuktu: West Africa's Great Trading Centre. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-04-c2.quote: Mansa Musa I was the ruler of the Mali Empire in West Africa from 1312 to 1337.
hafm-04-c2.claim: Mansa Musa ruled Mali from about 1312 to 1337; the dates are uncertain.

hafm-05-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Kilwa. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-05-c1.quote: Ibn Battuta (1304 - c. 1368 CE), who visited c. 1331 CE, to famously describe Kilwa as "one of the most beautiful towns in the world"
hafm-05-c1.claim: Ibn Battuta, visiting about 1331, called Kilwa one of the most beautiful and best-built towns in the world.
